direction: Keeping company: stored memory, a familiar landscape becoming uncertain, and midnight shadows as companionship. Three different visual densities and media; an interpretation selected for this rollout, not a claim about the original editorial theme.

items.title: The faces we keep
items.rationale: The poem contrasts changing, estranged life outside with faces suspended in an album. Show the act of keeping memory without inventing the people in those photographs.

review.notes: Normal-size review: the closed album is the emotional focus, partly occluded by the trunk lip. Lid hinge and box perspective read coherently; diffuse light falls into the recess. Broad gouache planes retain selective cloth detail without displaying invented faces or text. Warmth survives the restrained palette. No correction required; same-assistant review.

items.alt: A closed red-brown album rests inside an open wooden trunk beside folded cotton cloth, painted in quiet gouache.

items.title: Before the paths disappear
items.rationale: The village poem turns from labour and familiar fields toward unease at dusk. Suggest that threshold without exoticising villagers, identifying a real location, or inventing a threatening animal.

review.notes: Normal-size review: receding irregular field boundaries and a subdued low hill establish ordinary terrain at dusk. Foreground pastel strokes give way to flatter distant washes. Warm horizon remains restrained with no theatrical sun or invented villagers/wildlife. Familiarity and mild uncertainty fit the final turn of the poem; landscape is interpretive, not a claimed Nilagiri record.

items.alt: Charcoal and pastel fields lose their distant boundaries beneath low hills and a fading dusk sky.

items.title: Company in the night
items.rationale: Haflong treats midnight shadows as supportive company and introspection rather than fear. Keep the comforting ambiguity in physical foliage shadows; do not depict spirits, dream figures or a literal rainbow.

review.notes: Normal-size review: overlapping indigo leaf shadows read as gentle company, without faces or supernatural figures. Varied edge softness is plausible for foliage at different distances; jamb and single directional light anchor the abstract wash. Empty wall gives breathing room. Cool restrained palette differs from the album and field compositions; no correction needed.

items.alt: Soft indigo leaf shadows cross a pale wall beside the edge of a wooden window.

text_led.rationale: The short marital contrast is strongest as a compact verbal turn; a wedding vignette would prescribe the interpretation.
The shift from literary imitation to personal voice should be encountered directly in its ten lines, without a stock writing desk.
Keep the questions addressed to Time open; neither a clock nor an hourglass adds meaning.
